Marissa / Kim — I can take the topology and config snippets. Draft plan below and attached is v1 of the diagram.

Draft topology summary (high level):
- Lattice concept: we call this the "Guardian Lattice" — a set of discrete network zones (Control Plane, Dedicated Tenant Pools, Private VPC Enclaves, Shared Services). Each zone has strict ingress/egress contracts and explicit routing ACLs.
- Control Plane: hosted in our management region; communicates to Dedicated hosts over a one-way, authenticated control channel; control plane egress is tightly proxied and does not accept inbound traffic from tenant networks.
- Dedicated Tenant Pools: GPU pools isolated per-customer by namespace and overlay; kernel-level namespaces + host-level VLAN segmentation; no cross-tenant L2/L3 unless explicit bridge requested and documented.
- Private VPC Enclaves: customer-managed VPCs connect via approved peering or transit with enforced route filters; service endpoints are published via NATed egress points with TLS mutual auth.
- Egress & Proxying: all egress from inference nodes funnels to our egress proxies (Envoy clusters) which enforce URL allowlists, TLS inspection exceptions per contract, and record flows to our logging pipeline (retention consistent with Verdant contract).
- KMS & Secrets: customer keys for Private deployments can be in-customer KMS or Redwood-managed customer key (BYOK). Key usage in inference runtime is ephemeral; master keys never leave HSM boundary.

Attachments included (drafts):
- [Attachment: guardian-lattice-topology-v1.png] (diagram, annotated zones, arrows show control channels)
- [Attachment: guardian-network-narrative-v1.pdf] (1.5 page narrative with bullet controls)
- sample config snippets inline:
  * egress proxy (Envoy) example: route
    - cluster: upstream_logging
    - routes: { match: "/logs/*", cluster: "elasticsearch" }
